Consideration of a "compromise" is typically focused on ensuring that no one group is disproportionately benefiting at the expense of another. Thus, the proposal where the years are equally distributed among the groups should be the fairest. 

Given this, the best compromise in this situation would be (A) Proposal one, as it allocates an equal outcome to each group.
A

The ultimate goal is to create the best balance that would benefit all groups involved. 

In Proposal One, group apple-🍎 is greatly benefitted, but group bee-🐝 and group cow-🐮 are minimally affected. 

In Proposal Two, group bee-🐝 is most benefitted, with group cow-🐮 also gaining a modest benefit, but group apple-🍎 receives little benefit.

Proposal Three, however, gives a considerable amount of benefit to all groups. Group apple-🍎 and group cow-🐮 receive identical benefits, while group bee-🐝 receives a higher benefit. 

Therefore, the best compromise in this situation would be (C) Proposal three, as it provides a notable benefit to all groups involved.
C

Let's consider that a good compromise will balance the interests of all groups such that no single group faces a disproportionately low or high outcome.

In Proposal one, groups bee-🐝 and cow-🐮 have considerably better outcomes than group apple-🍎.

In Proposal two, group bee-🐝 has an advantageous outcome, while groups apple-🍎 and cow-🐮 have much lower ones.

In Proposal three, group apple-🍎 has a better outcome, while groups bee-🐝 and cow-🐮 are worse off.

None of the proposals offers an equal outcome to all groups, but Proposal one offers the best trade-off, with two groups sharing the same, higher outcome while one group receives a lower one.

Therefore, the best compromise in this situation would be (A) Proposal one.
